newsitem.title: UK: European bunker prices slide in strong competition.
newsitem.headline: European bunker prices slide in strong competition.

text.p: Bunker prices continued to fall in line with weaker spot and futures markets for both fuel oil and crude, despite some fairly good buying interest from shipowners at these lower levels, traders said.

Some traders felt the selloff had been somewhat overdone against the reasonable demand for product at European ports. They said prices had gapped lower amid aggressive competition for business and saw room for improvement once the scramble is over.
High and low sulphur fuels at most ports were marked around $5-$7 a tonne lower as spot fuel oil prices tumbled.
Diesel and gas oil bunkers were similarly weaker as gas oil futures continued under pressure.
Trade in European ports remained fairly active but aggressive selling saw buyers holding the upper hand continuing to cover requirements only when prices dipped lower.
In ARA Hamburg range bunker prices were $5-7 a tonne lower, but losses in Mediterranean markets were less harsh, with healthy Spanish demand supportive.
Prices in French, Italian and Greek ports eased $2-3 tonne while Egyptian, Fujairah and South African bunkers added a further $1-2 to Wednesday's losses.
